text:
Connor Hellebuyck is a Devil because he wanted out of Winnipeg badly enough to force it: the standoff with the Jets ended in the Oct 23 trade, and he has been in New Jersey's net for eight games since, at .913 and 2.4 goals saved above expected. That makes New Jersey's season a bet on him in the spring, and our playoff race already has them at 96%. They control play better than almost anyone, 56% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals are the quality of chances).

The worry is depth and special teams. Anthony Mantha (throat fracture surgery, per reports) and Johnathan Kovacevic are out at least a month. Connor Brown has taken Mantha's spot beside Evan Rodrigues and Jesper Boqvist and is up to 17:38 a night. The Hockey News' Mike Fink noted the Devils' penalty kill sits at 66.7%, far below league average, and this is the start of five games in eight days. Bratt has a nine-game point streak and Jack Hughes, whom our numbers call due, is our likeliest Devils scorer at 37%.

The Blues have won four of five and earned it, with more of the expected goals in four of those games. Joel Hofer has quietly taken the net: .923 on the season and .933 over his last five. That matters because Jordan Binnington, the goalie who won them a Cup, is now the subject of trade talk and headlines about his form. Justin Barron is the surprise, eight points in ten with the chances to back it, and Jimmy Snuggerud plays his 100th game.

Their first meeting, on Nov 5, went to the Devils 5-4 in overtime, a game New Jersey deserved 83% of the time. St. Louis sits at 42% in our playoff race, close enough that nights against the East's best are the measuring stick.
headline: Hellebuyck's new team visits a Blues side finding itself
